`EN-us`, `e` | `en`, `eng`, `EN-us` | `en`, `EN-us` | `en`, `EN-us` | | `//p[lang('e')]` | all four | `e` | `e` | | `//p[lang('en-US')]` | `EN-us` | `EN-us` | `EN-us` | https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-10/#function-lang > The [lang](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-10/#function-lang) function > returns true or false depending on whether the language of the context > node as specified by xml:lang attributes is the same as or is a > sublanguage of the language specified by the argument string. The > language of the context node is determined by the value of the xml:lang > attribute on the context node, or, if the context node has no xml:lang > attribute, by the value of the xml:lang attribute on the nearest > ancestor of the context node that has an xml:lang attribute. If there is > no such attribute, then > [lang](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-10/#function-lang) returns false. If > there is such an attribute, then > [lang](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-10/#function-lang) returns true if > the attribute value is equal to the argument ignoring case, or if there > is some suffix starting with - such that the attribute value is equal to > the argument ignoring that suffix of the attribute value and ignoring > case. For example, lang("en") would return true if the context node is > any of these five elements: > > ```xml > >
> > > ``` The new test sits next to `test_lang`; it fails on master and passes here. `ruby -Ilib test/run.rb` passes on Ruby 3.4 (also with `--enable-frozen-string-literal`), and the lang tests pass on 2.7. mutate the text node while pretty printing (#371) `Pretty#write_text` (`lib/rexml/formatters/pretty.rb:88-91`) calls the destructive `gsub!` and `squeeze!` on what `Text#to_s` hands back, and `Text#to_s` returns the node's own string — `@string` when `@raw`, otherwise the memoized `@normalized`: ```ruby def to_s return @string if @raw @normalized ||= Text::normalize( @string, doctype, @entity_filter ) end ``` So pretty printing permanently rewrites the document it is printing. Through `Document#write`, the documented pretty-print entry point: ```ruby d = REXML::Document.new("hello world") d.write(out, 2) d.to_s # before: "hello world" <- the source had three spaces # after: "hello world" ``` It is not only spaces. Measured the same way: | source | `to_s` after `write(out, 2)` on master | |---|---| | `hello world` | `hello world` | | `x & y` | `x & y` | | `line1\nline2` | `line1 line2` | With a `@raw` text node, `Text#value` itself changes. ### The other four call sites `grep -n "node\.to_s" lib/rexml/formatters/*.rb` gives five results. Four of them — `transitive.rb:54`, `default.rb:94`, `default.rb:99`, `default.rb:105` — are `output << node.to_s`, treating the return value as read-only. `pretty.rb` was the only one writing to it. The change is to use the non-destructive `gsub` and `squeeze`.
